sources.cite: Alfa Laval, Grundfos by Alfa Laval plate heat exchangers, maintenance manual 200019583-2-EN-GB (2026-07): main components pp. 16-18, bolt configuration p. 35, opening (steps 1-15) pp. 45-48, torque p. 49, closing (steps 1-17) pp. 50-52, plates out and in p. 55

frame_plate.name: Frame plate
frame_plate.does: The fixed plate, with the portholes and the four connections to the pipes. The plate package is pressed against it; it stays on its foundation with its pipes on when the exchanger is opened.

pressure_plate.name: Pressure plate
pressure_plate.does: The moveable plate that compresses the plate package against the frame plate. It hangs from the carrying bar and is pushed back along it to open the package.

carrying_bar.name: Carrying bar
carrying_bar.does: Carries the plate package and the pressure plate. Its sliding surfaces are cleaned and greased before the pressure plate is moved.

guiding_bar.name: Guiding bar
guiding_bar.does: Keeps all the plates aligned at their lower end.

support_column.name: Support column
support_column.does: Supports the carrying bar and the guiding bar at their far end.

end_plate_2.name: End plate II
end_plate_2.does: The plate next to the frame plate, the first one hung on the carrying bar when the package is closed.
end_plate_2.material: Stainless steel plate with its gasket

plates.name: Channel plates
plates.does: The plates that transfer heat: the two fluids flow in the channels between them, every other channel each. Each plate carries a gasket that seals between the channels and to the surroundings.
plates.material: Stainless steel plates with elastomer gaskets

end_plate_1.name: End plate I
end_plate_1.does: The plate next to the pressure plate, the first one off when the package is opened.
end_plate_1.material: Stainless steel plate with its gasket

text: The frame plate stays on its foundation, its pipes connected.
why: All four connections are on the frame plate here, so the package opens without undoing a pipe; pipes on a pressure plate are taken off first (opening, step 3).

text: The support column stays where it stands.
why: If there is a support foot under the guiding bar, it stays where it is (opening, step 7).

text: The carrying bar stays between the frame plate and the support column: wipe its sliding surfaces clean and grease them.
why: Opening, step 4: the pressure plate slides along it.
needs: frame_plate
The carrying bar hangs from the frame plate.
The frame plate stays.
support_column
The carrying bar rests on the support column.
The support column stays.

text: The guiding bar stays between the frame plate and the support column.
needs: frame_plate
The guiding bar is fixed to the frame plate.
The frame plate stays.
support_column
The guiding bar rests on the support column.
The support column stays.

text: Hang End plate II on the carrying bar, against the frame plate.
why: Check first that every gasket sits in its groove and every sealing surface is clean (closing, steps 1 and 3).
needs: carrying_bar
The plates hang from the carrying bar.
Take the plates off before the carrying bar.
guiding_bar
The guiding bar keeps the plates in line at the bottom.
Take the plates off before the guiding bar.

text: Hang the channel plates one by one, in the order and the way round the plate hanging list gives, each pressed towards the frame plate by its upper part.
why: Taking them out, each plate is lifted off by itself, by hand or with a lifting device for large ones, never by the edges round its portholes (p. 55). The diagonal line drawn on the package before it was opened shows when a plate is out of order.
needs: end_plate_2
The channel plates go against End plate II.
Take the channel plates off before End plate II.

text: Hang End plate I last, next to where the pressure plate comes.
needs: plates
End plate I goes against the last channel plate.
End plate I comes off first.

text: Push the pressure plate along the carrying bar against the plate package and press the package together.
why: Opening, step 13: the pressure plate is pushed gently away from the frame plate once the bolts are out.
needs: end_plate_1
The pressure plate closes the package: hang all the plates first.
Push the pressure plate back before the plates come off.

text: Put the tightening bolts in place and tighten them crosswise until the package measures 1.2 times the A-measurement, the frame plate and the pressure plate kept parallel; then let the package rest for an hour if possible.
why: Closing, steps 5 to 8. Opening, steps 9 to 12: the threads brushed and greased, the bolts loosened keeping the plates parallel (no more than 10 mm skew across, 25 mm up and down), then taken out. The A-measurement, noted before opening (step 6), is what counts, not the torque (p. 49).
needs: pressure_plate
The tightening bolts pull the pressure plate in: push it against the package first.
Take the tightening bolts out before the pressure plate is pushed back.

text: Put the locking bolts in place, then tighten all the bolts crosswise until the A-measurement is reached.
why: Closing, steps 9 and 10, then the protection sheets, the pipes and the pressure plate's feet back on and a hydrostatic test (steps 13 to 16). Opening starts here: the exchanger cooled to about 40 °C and drained, the protection sheets off, a diagonal line drawn on the package, the A-measurement noted, the feet at the pressure plate off (steps 1 to 7), then the locking bolts out (step 8).
needs: tightening_bolts
The locking bolts go in at 1.2 times the A-measurement, after the tightening bolts.
Take the locking bolts out before the tightening bolts are loosened.
